A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same guided-search research, despite the changed title and method name. All 20 pages of v1 and 19 pages of v2, including appendices A–F, support comparison. Changed models and protocols limit direct numerical performance comparisons, not document comparability.

before.justification: v1 reports original Countdown experiments, including accuracy comparisons, node-selection ablations, and operation-level PPO analyses, with additional experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original Countdown experiments and code self-repair results on CodeContests and CodeForces, including token-budget curves and pass@k tables.

M1.justification: Guided-ReST retains GSoS's subgoal replacement and trajectory truncation mechanism. However, v2 changes PPO from GAE with KL regularization to Monte Carlo returns without a KL penalty, and replaces the correctness/efficiency reward with a binary outcome reward. Section 4 and Algorithm 3 add an episode-level code-repair adaptation using reference-solution feedback, masking reference code during training and supervising only the final response.

E1.justification: Countdown with seen and unseen targets remains. v2 adds multi-turn code self-repair, training on 16K SYNTHETIC-1 problems curated from APPS, CodeContests, and TACO, and evaluating on CodeContests and CodeForces. This substantially broadens the domain and task requirements beyond arithmetic tree search.

E2.justification: The Countdown comparison adds a reported behavior-cloning result below 40% accuracy in v2 Section 5.2 and omits v1's evaluated Symbolic baseline from Figure 4. SoS and PPO remain; the earlier STaR self-training baseline corresponds to ReST rather than constituting a newly added comparator.

E3.justification: Countdown switches from GPT-2 250M to Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, with revised training budgets and hyperparameters. PPO changes from 25,600 sampled training problems to 200K examples over two epochs. Evaluation adds token-budget sweeps and pass@k; Table 1 uses 10K rather than 200K problems. New code experiments use Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, four-turn episodes, 16K-token responses, and private-test execution, without RL fine-tuning.

E4.justification: v2 adds pass@k candidate-coverage analysis and evaluates operation-level PPO and dense rewards across token budgets. It removes v1's First/Rand/Last node-selection sensitivity study, trajectory likelihood/length distributions, value-learning and KL-stability diagnostics, and numerical GPT-Neo/GPT-2 and APA appendix comparisons. These are substantial changes to the diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly reports three training seeds, means, standard deviations, and error bars in Section 4.1, Figure 4, and Table 2. v2 provides point estimates without corresponding seed counts or uncertainty intervals. Its 32 or 128 sampled responses per problem do not establish repeated training runs; the change is a removal of uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The Countdown results are replaced under changed conditions: v1 Table 2 reports GSoS+PPO at 74.77%/73.30% for seen/unseen targets, while v2 reports approximately 87% for both. This is not a same-setting performance gain. New pass@k results include Guided-ReST versus ReST pass@32 of 33.9% versus 30.4% on CodeContests and 37.6% versus 35.9% on CodeForces in v2 Table 3. Multiple earlier diagnostic result sets disappear.

T1.justification: The formal value-training target changes from GAE-based returns in v1 Appendix D to Monte Carlo returns in v2 Section 3.3, and Section 4 defines episode-level solution/feedback sequences. The operation-level probability factorization already exists in v1; expressing it as a log importance ratio is equivalent mathematics. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion expand from Countdown accuracy and guided-training/PPO synergy to inference-time search efficiency and applicability to code self-repair. v2 makes a new central claim of comparable accuracy using roughly half PPO's token budget. The underlying claim that optimal-solution guidance improves learned search is retained.

C2.justification: v2 explains PPO synergy through broader coverage of correct candidates measured by pass@k, replacing the earlier emphasis on training stability and contextual likelihood tradeoffs. It adds substantive limitations concerning access to optimal solutions and an oracle capable of locating errors and backtracking. It also discusses the modest code-repair gains and acknowledges that RL fine-tuning on code was not tested.

D1.justification: v2 adds code-generation, repair, reference-guidance, and reference-masking prompts, together with code sampling settings. Appendix E replaces the TRIL-based implementation description with verl, Liger Kernel, and vLLM, and revises training and hardware details. Earlier GPT-2 configuration and implementation-bug disclosures are omitted. The repository address changes, and v2's release statement mentions source code without v1's explicit trained-model availability statement.

R1.justification: v2 substantially repositions the work around test-time compute, jump-start RL, and episode-level self-correction. It introduces JSRL as methodological inspiration and identifies Chang et al.'s guided-generation work as the closest predecessor, distinguishing multiple guide–base interactions. The earlier related-work discussion claiming an on-policy extension of higher-level MDP methods is removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, methods narrative, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. GSoS becomes Guided-ReST, preliminary fine-tuning sections are consolidated, a separate code-repair section is introduced, and the experiments and appendices are reorganized. These changes substantially alter the document's narrative beyond adding experimental content.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are redrawn, and the empirical presentation shifts from fixed-budget bar charts to accuracy-versus-token-budget curves. v2 introduces pass@k tables and four code-prompt panels while removing several diagnostic plots. Retained appendix search-trace examples are restyled and renumbered, rather than being new evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens applicability and evaluation beyond v1's synthetic Countdown setting: code-repair experiments test a practical adaptation, while token-budget curves and pass@k analyses directly examine efficiency and candidate coverage. These address important gaps in the earlier evidence. The gains outweigh the loss of seed-based uncertainty reporting and several diagnostic ablations, although those losses weaken confidence. Code RL benefits remain untested, and the higher Countdown scores cannot establish improvement under unchanged conditions because models and training settings changed.
